summary:
CrewReady: Beyond Us is a free browser game that trains children aged 7–12 to think like mission engineers, for the challenge "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer". Earth is too full, so the player commands a crew to Mars across six levels. Every choice trades one of four meters (Power, Air & Water, Food, Shield) against another, so kids learn the key rule of space engineering: protecting one thing always costs another. Twinkle, a friendly robot, introduces each level and gives hints that link to the NASA source.

Real data drives the game. NASA DONKI space-weather records set the size of the in-game solar storm, and NOAA's planetary K-index sets the speed of the Fly runner. Real photos, Mars weather and an ISS lettuce study from NASA fill the story, and every fact shows its source.

It matters because many children never meet real space science in a form they can play. CrewReady works offline in English and Bangla, collects no personal data, and runs on a phone, so any classroom can use it.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

CrewReady: Beyond Us is a free browser game. The player leads a crew from a crowded Earth to Mars across six levels: The Last Departure, The Dangerous Journey, First Breath, The Dust Storm, Grow or Go Hungry and Crew Up. Four meters (Power, Air & Water, Food, Shield) trade against each other, and any meter at zero puts the mission in danger. Kids play as Orbit or Nova, guided by Twinkle, a robot who explains words and gives hints with NASA source links. If a mission fails, Mission Replay shows which choice cost the most, without blame, and the player tries again. Each level has a bonus mini-game, and there is an endless runner called Fly and a Space Arcade. Players earn Stardust to spend on hints.

HOW IT ANSWERS THE CHALLENGE

The challenge asks for a trainer that teaches how a mission balances competing demands. Our core idea is one honest rule a child can feel: protecting one thing costs another. More shielding means less food. Calling Earth costs air and water. Mars is far away, so the crew must decide on their own.

HOW REAL NASA DATA SHAPES THE GAME

- Storm size: recent geomagnetic storms from NASA DONKI set the in-game storm as Small, Medium or Large. A bigger real storm costs the crew more. Level 6 always uses the stronger of the live storm and the archived May 2024 superstorm.

- Runner speed: today's NOAA planetary K-index sets the Fly runner's starting speed.

- Real facts and pictures: EPIC (Earth from deep space), InSight (Mars weather), OSDR (lettuce grown on the ISS), NeoWs (asteroids NASA tracks), APOD, the NASA Image Library and NTRS.

- Honest labels: a NASA LIVE or NASA ARCHIVE badge shows which data is on screen. The Sources page separates what is real from what is fiction made for the story.

Limits: live storm size uses the Kp reading only. If DONKI has no recent storm, or the player is offline, the game uses the archived May 2024 superstorm. So the challenge changes with space weather, not with how well the player plays.

HOW IT WORKS AND WHAT WE USED

A static progressive web app built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Zustand, Tailwind CSS and Three.js. The rules are pure TypeScript functions with 200+ automated tests (Vitest, Playwright). The NASA service waits 3 seconds, caches the answer, then falls back to NASA snapshots saved in the project. A service worker caches the game, so after one online visit it works offline, and it can be installed to a home screen. There is no backend, no ads, no trackers and no personal data. The game works in English and Bangla. Videos were made with Remotion.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Children learn systems thinking and real space science through play. Schools with weak internet can still use it. Bangla support opens it to children across Bangladesh and South Asia. A "Use it in class" section gives teachers one key lesson per level.

CREATIVITY

Real space weather decides how hard the storm hits. Mission Replay turns a failure into a lesson, not a punishment. Twinkle's hints always point back to the NASA source.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Child safety and privacy first. Honesty about what is real and what is fiction. Simple words and large touch targets for young players. A game that works offline and on a phone. We also tested informally with children, and one early tester said it was too hard, so we simplified the text and added explain cards. We have not run a formal study.

WHAT WE WOULD BUILD NEXT

Use live solar particle and CME speed data for storm size, add a score for how well players balance the meters, add more NASA data such as Mars dust and NASA POWER solar data, run a classroom study with teachers, finish the Bangla review, and add a teacher guide.

USE OF AI

Claude (Anthropic) helped write and review code, tests and drafts. Google Gemini and Antigravity helped with videos and some modules. ChatGPT image generation made the character and welcome art. The team created the idea, the story, the six-level design, the meter balance, the data choices and the videos. Full details: docs/AI_USE.md in our repository.
